title: Ordering at a restaurant
setting: A small neighbourhood restaurant, no English menu. You're on your own and you can't eat eggs.

n1.speaker: staff
n1.japanese: いらっしゃいませ。何名様ですか。
n1.english: Welcome. How many in your party?
n1.audioHint: いらっしゃいませ。なんめいさまですか

options.feedback: Holding up one finger alongside is completely normal and not childish here.
For two. Remember 一人 and 二人 are irregular — ひとり and ふたり, not いちにん/ににん.

n2.speaker: staff
n2.japanese: カウンター席へどうぞ。お飲み物は何になさいますか。
n2.romaji: Kauntā seki e dōzo. O-nomimono wa nani ni nasaimasu ka.
n2.english: Counter seat, this way. What would you like to drink?
n2.audioHint: カウンターせきへどうぞ。おのみものはなにになさいますか

options.japanese: ビールをお願いします。
options.feedback: 生 (nama, draft) is what you'll usually get if you just say 生ビール.
Water is free everywhere and nobody will think anything of it.
They asked about drinks specifically. You'll get the menu, but answering the question asked keeps the rhythm.

n3.speaker: staff
n3.japanese: ご注文はお決まりですか。
n3.audioHint: ごちゅうもんはおきまりですか

options.feedback: Lead with the allergy before ordering, not after. This is the right moment.
Asking for a recommendation is a good move in a small place — but flag the allergy first.

options.english: This one, please. (pointing at the menu)
options.feedback: You've ordered without mentioning the eggs. Fine for a preference, genuinely risky for an allergy — say it before you order, every time.

n3b.speaker: staff
n3b.japanese: かしこまりました。親子丼ですね。
n3b.audioHint: かしこまりました。おやこどんですね

options.feedback: Caught it in time. 親子丼 is chicken *and egg* — the name literally means 'parent and child'. Exactly the trap that flagging the allergy first avoids.
Good instinct. Asking what's in a dish catches hidden ingredients — dashi, egg, wheat — that the name doesn't advertise.

n4.speaker: staff
n4.japanese: 卵ですね。承知しました。こちらは大丈夫です。
n4.romaji: Tamago desu ne. Shōchi shimashita. Kochira wa daijōbu desu.
n4.english: Eggs, understood. This one here is fine.
n4.audioHint: たまごですね。しょうちしました。こちらはだいじょうぶです

options.japanese: じゃあ、それをお願いします。
options.feedback: じゃあ = 'in that case'. A small word that makes you sound much more fluent than it costs.
Warranted — they checked the dish for you rather than shrugging.

n5.speaker: staff
n5.japanese: お待たせしました。どうぞ。
n5.english: Sorry to keep you waiting. Here you are.
n5.audioHint: おまたせしました。どうぞ

options.feedback: Said to nobody in particular before you start. Skipping it is the noticeable thing.
Fine, though いただきます is what a Japanese diner would say at this exact moment.

n6.speaker: staff
n6.japanese: お会計はレジでお願いします。
n6.romaji: O-kaikei wa reji de onegai shimasu.
n6.audioHint: おかいけいはレジでおねがいします

options.feedback: The bookend to いただきます, said on the way out. It lands as genuine thanks and staff notice it.
Worth asking at a small independent place — plenty are still cash-only.

end.speaker: narration
end.english: Fed, and no eggs. The lesson worth keeping: state a dietary restriction *before* ordering, not after the dish is named.
